definition: Literally 'candies'; light euphemistic slang for the testicles, emphasizing their round, soft shape.
notes: The confectionery connotation makes this notably milder than 'couilles'; favored in playful or childlike registers.

definition: Very crude French argot for the testicles; used in low-register and criminal slang, possibly of Romani origin.
notes: Deep argot with limited contemporary recognition; not found in standard dictionaries; survives mainly in bawdy oral tradition and older argot glossaries.

definition: Literally 'nut' or 'walnut'; informal slang for the testicles by shape analogy, parallel to English 'nuts'.
notes: Typically used in plural; the singular 'noix' in a non-sexual context means a light head-flick, making context essential.

definition: Literally 'family jewels'; the standard French euphemism for the testicles, treating them as cherished patrilineal heirlooms.
notes: The identical idiom exists in English; universally understood across all generations and social registers; essentially non-vulgar.

definition: The clinical anatomical term for the external opening of the rectum; borrowed directly from Latin, used identically in French medicine.
notes: Perfect cognate with English; standard in medical, educational, and public health contexts; carries no vulgar charge.

definition: The terminal section of the large intestine running from the sigmoid colon to the anus; anatomical Latin term used identically in French medicine.
notes: Perfect cognate; from Latin 'intestinum rectum' (straight intestine); used exclusively in clinical and educational discourse in French.

definition: The external anal sphincter muscle controlling closure of the anal canal; standard two-word anatomical term in French medicine.
notes: Adjective follows noun per standard French morphology ('sphincter anal' not 'anal sphincter'); recognition lower than 'anus' due to greater technical specificity.

definition: The anatomical region of tissue between the genitals and the anus; the French clinical term for the perineum.
notes: Recognition has increased through obstetric public health campaigns (massage périnéal, rééducation périnéale postpartum); still largely confined to medical and post-natal contexts.

definition: The standard coarse French term for the buttocks or ass; by extension the anus; the semantic range mirrors English 'ass'.
notes: Primarily denotes the posterior as a whole rather than specifically the anus; embedded in hundreds of idioms (en avoir plein le cul, tête de cul, etc.); the foundational unit of French anal vocabulary.

definition: Literally 'hole of the ass'; the primary crude French term for the anus, and a very common insult for a contemptible person.
notes: Fully parallel to English 'asshole' in both anatomical and insult functions; one of the most versatile expletives in colloquial French.

definition: Crude French argot for the anus; also appears innocuously in the set phrase 'coup de fion' meaning a final polishing touch.
notes: 'Coup de fion' (a finishing flourish) is a standard expression in French; speakers who know the argot sense perceive an unintended double entendre.

definition: Literally 'washer' or 'flat ring'; slang for the anus derived from the circular shape of the anal sphincter.
notes: The mechanical hardware metaphor (plumbing/engineering washer) gives it a detached quality that lowers perceived vulgarity relative to more evocative terms.

definition: Literally 'lozenge' or 'small disc'; dated slang for the anus based on the small round shape of the anal opening.
notes: Has largely fallen from active use; feels quaint and humorously old-fashioned to contemporary French speakers; peak use roughly mid-20th century.

definition: Literally 'onion'; slang for the anus referencing the concentric layered appearance of the sphincter when viewed externally.
notes: Unrelated to the idiom 'ce sont mes oignons' (that's my business); the sexual meaning requires context and is not the primary sense of the word.

definition: Old French argot for the buttocks or posterior; derived from 'derrière' via argot phonological transformation; roughly equivalent to 'arse'.
notes: Primarily denotes the buttocks rather than specifically the anus; strongly associated with 19th–early 20th century criminal and working-class argot; uncommon in contemporary speech.

definition: Very crude French argot for the anus; a compound emphasizing the orifice nature, built from 'trou' (hole) with a pejorative augmentative suffix.
notes: Low contemporary recognition; survives in bawdy oral tradition and older argot literature; etymology of the '-fignard' suffix is contested, possibly related to 'figne' (anus in some dialects).

definition: Archaic French criminal and ecclesiastical argot for the anus or posterior; possibly derived from monastic bawdy wordplay on liturgical prose writing.
notes: Found in 19th-century French argot dictionaries (Vidocq, Delvau); essentially extinct in living speech; the co-occurrence with ordinary 'prose' (literary writing) creates comic ambiguity in older texts.

definition: Literally 'little rose'; common French slang for the anus, referencing the puckered rose-like appearance of the sphincter at rest.
notes: Has partial technical overlap: 'chute de la rosette' is a clinical descriptor for rectal prolapse; this dual register is unusual among anal slang terms.

definition: Literally 'bullet hole'; crude French slang for the anus, comparing the small round opening to a bullet wound.
notes: 'Balle' is bullet, not ball (sport), making the metaphor distinctly martial; in military argot 'trou de balle' was also used as a general insult for enlisted men.

definition: Archaic French criminal and ecclesiastical argot for the anus or posterior; possibly derived from monastic bawdy wordplay on liturgical prose writing.
notes: Duplicate entry in source data. Essentially extinct in living speech; found in 19th-century argot dictionaries; see record 17 for full notes.

definition: The standard French clinical term for coitus; sexual intercourse between two people, prototypically penile-vaginal penetration.
notes: Slightly more formal and literary than 'rapport sexuel' in everyday usage; preferred in legal, medical, and journalistic registers.

definition: The French term for copulation; sexual union between two individuals; used primarily in biological, zoological, and medical contexts.
notes: In French as in English, 'copulation' carries a distinctly zoological register and is more naturally applied to animals than humans in everyday speech.

definition: The standard everyday French phrase for sexual intercourse; used in medical, journalistic, educational, and conversational contexts alike.
notes: The de facto neutral default term in French for penetrative sex; spans clinical through conversational registers and is used by physicians and teenagers alike.

definition: Literally 'sexual act'; a formal French phrase covering any sexual activity, frequently used in legal and clinical contexts to denote intercourse.
notes: Semantically broader than 'coït' (which specifies penetration); 'acte sexuel' is the standard term in the French Penal Code for criminally relevant sexual conduct.

definition: Sexual penetration; the insertion of the penis or an object into a bodily orifice; used in both clinical and everyday French with near-universal recognition.
notes: In French law, 'pénétration sexuelle' is the definitional element of rape ('viol'), giving the term a heavier forensic weight than its English cognate carries in common usage.
